runner: omp (Oh My Pi) v18.1.13, --no-tools --no-lsp, one session per seat

findings.what: The mutation operator set is five call-site prefixes (`demand(`, `errors.push(`, `reasons.push(`, `findings.push(`, `problems.push(`), i.e. it only neuters the emission of a refusal that is already reached; it cannot mutate the predicate that decides whether the guard fires (comparisons, boundary conditions, ordering, CAS expected-old values), so '514/514 killed, 0 survivors' proves the tests notice a deleted refusal push, not that the guards are correctly conditioned — the headline number is much weaker than the word 'mutation' implies.

findings.where: section 5 mutation table vs. sections 3/4 — coverage denominator
findings.what: 49 modules are mutated but 38 contracts define 389 refusal classes and the package gives no mapping from class to a killed mutant, so there is no evidence that every declared refusal class is producible or exercised; conspicuously, `src/host/doctor-checks.mjs` reports 0 mutants/0 killed while `security.signer_boundary` (01-core-flows.md §2) is the mechanism that mechanically stops model launch, and `src/host/*` has no module named for arena, debate, autobuild, housekeeping, walkthrough, reflect-cost-watch, human-decision, refusal-vocabulary, platform-support, sdk-write-api, artifact-write-receipt, static-analysis, integration-authorization or bounded-loop — contracts whose classes therefore have no shown evaluator.

Four of twenty groups are run without a paired silent control, and the package's own stated reason for controls ('a guard that refuses everything would detect every fault and mean nothing by it') applies exactly to them; the coverage line nevertheless reports `covered_by_real_fault=20; complete=true`, so the summary asserts completeness at a strength only 16 rows actually support — F004 (identity swap) in particular is the runtime-identity guard, the highest-value place for a false-positive check.

The whole user-authority chain rests on `UserDecisionRecord` being unforgeable by the model, and the design admits the only enforcement is a probe that 'не доказывает изоляцию', with platform attestation named as deferred — yet §5 states flatly 'Deployment without enforceable boundary ... blocks model launch' and §2's doctor check treats an undeclared boundary as `unverifiable`; a declared-but-unattested endpoint therefore passes, so the guarantee that no model can mint `actor=user` has no mechanism, only a self-report from the daemon whose own boundary is in question.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §2 ('До issue #14 закрытый path-role classifier...') vs. 02-architecture.md §7 ('Кодовый кандидат')
findings.what: The five-way path-role classifier is declared unreachable in the shipped system ('в поставляемой системе пятизначный classifier недостижим') because the registry decides, yet the same paragraph keeps it as the normative rule for `governance_mapping_sidecar` / `additional_normative` / `unknown` and the park reason `artifact_mapping_required`; a rule that is simultaneously normative and unreachable leaves those park classes with no producer, and the reconciliation is prose rather than a check anything evaluates.

findings.where: section 5, 'What is not claimed' — issue #10 criterion 2
findings.what: Deferring the declarative workflow graph is a defect in *this* design, not a neutral scheduling choice: 01-core-flows.md §8 encodes the resume state machine as a ~45-row prose table mapping park reason to workflow step, and §7/§5 encode ordering invariants the same way, so with no machine-checkable graph nothing validates that every one of the 389 refusal classes has a reachable owning step, that `onTransit` rejects exactly the mismatches the table names, or that the table and the implemented steps have not drifted — the package's own `refusal_vocabulary_unknown_step` class presumes a step registry the graph would have supplied.

`npm test` is reported only as 1809 pass / 0 fail with no coverage figure, no assertion-per-contract mapping and no statement of what the suite does not reach, and the clean-room line reports ten steps as `ok` with no per-step assertion content; both are pass/fail totals presented in positions where the reader is invited to read them as adequacy, which is a claim outrunning what was run.

findings.where: section 5, 'Mutation' — 'A broader hand-run procedure was used ... its counts are in the pull requests'
findings.what: The package concedes two different mutation numbers exist and that the larger, broader one lives outside the reviewed version in pull requests that are not in section 3 and not digest-pinned; that number is therefore unreviewable from this package while still being offered as reassurance, and the reproducible number it is contrasted with is the narrow one flagged above.

findings.where: section 5, mutation module list vs. 02-architecture.md §2 and §4
findings.what: The daemon is explicitly outside the mutated set, yet the load-bearing primitives ADR-014/ADR-023/ADR-025 (atomic creation binding, signed authority/intent heads, workflow custody CAS) live there and are supplied by 31 pinned patches; the extension's guards can only be as strong as those primitives, so 'the daemon's guards are not mutated' is not a minor scope note but the exclusion of the layer that actually enforces the identities everything else binds to — and no equivalent fault injection against the patched daemon is shown beyond the four uncontrolled harness rows.

Only 2 of 115 files are reproduced in full; the 38 contracts are given as section-4 rule inventories (headings plus refusal-class names) which cannot show whether a section's body actually specifies an evaluable rule, so the panel is asked for a design verdict on 113 files it can only check by digest against a repository it cannot open.

Cross-family independence is the mechanism behind the panel gate, but 'family' is asserted by route-string convention (Codex and GPT declared one family in §6) with no artifact in section 3 that registers the family partition or is validated against the route table, so `arena_judge_family_conflict` and the Lead-selection rule depend on a mapping nothing in the pack pins.

seats.read: The whole panel package as delivered: section 1 (version, upstream commit + 31-patch series, digests), section 2 (the four questions), section 3 (all 115 path/digest rows, read as a table — I did not recompute the SHA-256 chain, having no tools), section 4 (all 38 contract entries, their section lists and all listed refusal classes), section 5 in full (test total, mutation method and per-module table of 49 modules, clean-room step list, the 20-row fault matrix with per-row evidence, and the 'what is not claimed' list), section 6 in full (`01-core-flows.md` and `02-architecture.md` end to end, including §2 alignment/policy, §5–§9 of core flows and §2, §4, §5, §7, §8 of architecture), and section 7's output shape. Findings are cross-references between these parts.
seats.not_read: I could not read and did not read: the bytes of the other 113 files in section 3 — all 38 contract bodies (only section 4's headings and refusal-class names were available), `03-technical-plan.md`, `04-decisions.md` (so ADR-014/023/025/029/030 are known only by reference), `README.md`, `compat/autosk/manifest.v1.json` and the 31 patches, and every JSON Schema and resource file including `refusal-vocabulary.v1.json`, `artifact-registry.v1.json`, `stage-carriers.v1.json` and `mutation-survivors.v1.json`. I did not run or verify anything: I did not recompute the candidate digest from section 3, did not verify the report digests, the clean-room tree hash or any file hash, did not run `npm test`, `node scripts/mutation-report.mjs` or the fault harness, and did not inspect any `src/host/*.mjs`, `test/*.test.mjs` or `scripts/*.mjs` source. Consequently my findings about operator scope, module-to-contract coverage and unpaired controls rest on the package's own descriptions rather than on the code.

findings.what: [INFERENCE] Отложена несущая гарантия: архитектура требует блокировать запуск модели без принудительной изоляции signer/secure store, но описанный security.signer_boundary проверяет лишь недоступность объявленного endpoint и самоотчёт демона, прямо не доказывая изоляцию, поэтому его успешность недостаточна для допуска, на котором основана исключительная пользовательская власть над approval, waiver и integration.

findings.where: Пакет §5, «The fault matrix, with its denominator», утверждение перед таблицей
findings.what: Утверждение «Each group is injected for real and paired with a control» противоречит последующему пояснению и таблице: парный контроль заявлен только для 16 из 20 групп, а F001–F004 явно имеют «not paired», поэтому универсальное утверждение о контролях необходимо сузить.

findings.where: Пакет §5, fault matrix: определение F004 и строка evidence для F004
findings.what: F004 определён как resume при изменённой runtime identity, однако приведённое свидетельство описывает сохранение pin уже допущенной задачи и новый pin следующего admission, не указывая фактический resume и результат его проверки, поэтому заявленное покрытие именно этого сценария представленным описанием не подтверждено.

findings.what: The candidate includes a closed Autobuild contract (15 host-enforced classes: budgets, independent generator/evaluator, no rubric mutation) but neither load-bearing design text sites a host Autobuild runtime, the mutation table has no autobuild module, and section 5 does not defer it the way it defers Sonar #47 and issue #10 criterion 2.

Load-bearing stops brief_alignment_required, core_flow_decision_required, tech_plan_readiness_required, alignment_policy_out_of_scope, alignment_record_stale, artifact_mapping_required, and protocol_lock_invalid are named in the core flow, yet none appear among the 389 contract refusal classes, while the sibling tickets_breakdown_alignment_required is in tickets-manifest.md — those gates are either narrative-only or have no contract owner visible in this package.

The two full texts disagree on the signer boundary: 01 states the doctor probe does not prove isolation and platform attestation is deferred, while 02 calls the same boundary an enforceable production property and a mandatory preflight assertion rather than a same-UID residual.

Coverage is declared complete=true with covered_by_real_fault=20, but F001–F004 were run without a paired silent control, so the matrix does not show that those guards stay quiet on the unfaulted state — the completeness claim is injection coverage, not specificity.
